terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here and read what Theo's functions do.

tasks.title: Keep the wrap inside the label
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/scope.js`, fix `labelLine(scent, giftWrap)` so it returns the scent, a comma and a space, then `gift wrapped` when `giftWrap` is true or `plain box` when it is false: `'Cedar, gift wrapped'`. Keep `wrap` inside the function.

Check calls `labelLine` with other scents, wrapped and plain, and makes sure `wrap` is not made at the top level of the file.
nextSteps: Run `node src/scope.js` and read the error: it names a line and a name.
Find where that name is made, and where it is used.
Make it once inside the function, where the `return` can see it.
Run the file again: the first line should be a label.
hints: `ReferenceError: wrap is not defined` means that at the `return`, no `wrap` can be seen from where it is used.
A name made with `let` inside `{ }` lives only until the closing brace. Both `wrap`s are gone before the `return`.
Write `let wrap` once at the start of the function, before the `if`, and in the two parts only give it its value: `wrap = '...'`.

tasks.title: Let the sale price out
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, fix `salePrice(priceCents, percentOff)` so it returns the price with `percentOff` percent taken off, rounded to whole cents. With a `percentOff` of 0 the price stays as it is.

Check calls `salePrice` with other prices and discounts, 0 included.
nextSteps: Run the file and look at what `salePrice(2000, 25)` prints.
Count how many names called `price` the function makes.
Make sure the sale price goes into the `price` the `return` hands back.
hints: The sum inside the `if` is right. The trouble is where its answer goes.
`let` inside the braces makes a second `price` that hides the first one until the closing brace. The `return` comes after it, so it sees the first.
Inside the `if`, give the outer `price` its new value without `let`: `price = Math.round(...)`.

tasks.title: Use the zone you are given
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, fix `shippingNote(zone)` so it returns `Hand delivered` for `'local'`, `Sent by courier` for `'national'`, and `Sent by air mail` for anywhere else, whatever `todaysZone` says.

Check calls `shippingNote` with each zone.
nextSteps: Run the file: Theo asked about an order abroad. What did he get?
Look at which name the questions inside `shippingNote` ask about.
Make the function decide on what it is given.
Run the file again and try other zones.
hints: `shippingNote` has a parameter, `zone`, but it never uses it.
A function can see names outside it, which is why this runs without an error. But then it answers about `todaysZone`, not about the order it was asked about.
In both questions, compare `zone` instead of `todaysZone`.

tasks.title: Hand the note back
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, fix `packingNote(weightGrams)` so it returns `Heavy box` for more than 1000 grams and `Light box` otherwise. It must give its note back with `return` and leave `lastNote` alone. You may delete `lastNote` once nothing uses it.

Check calls `packingNote` with heavy and light parcels, 1000 grams included, and makes sure `lastNote` does not change.
nextSteps: Run the file: what does `packingNote(1500)` print?
Notice the function writes its answer into a name outside it.
Give each note back with `return` instead.
Delete `lastNote` if nothing else uses it, and run the file.
hints: A function with no `return` gives back `undefined`, whatever it does inside.
Writing into a name outside the function means two parcels share one note, and the second overwrites the first. A function should hand its answer back.
In each part of the `if`, write `return 'Heavy box'` or `return 'Light box'` in place of the line that sets `lastNote`.
